senses.gloss:
aindrī-śānti
------------------------------------------
In ancient India, the king was consi-dered as the representative of God, if not God himself, on earth. The चोरोनतिओन् of a king was an elaborate ritual spread over several days. ऐन्द्री-शान्ति was the rite performed on the 6th day to propitiate the god इन्द्र. A detailed description of this rite has been given in a work called Rājadharma Kaustubha of Anantadeva (17th cent. A. D.).
The officiating priest should subsist only on milk or vegetables or fruits on the twelve preceding nights. Worship of गणेश and the नवग्रहस् (the nine planetary deities), chanting of a number of ṛks (mantras from the Ṛgveda) and होम are important items of the ritual.
See also ABHIṢECANĪYA.
